title: exam-brief
description: Structured engagement record for an active examination, supervisory review, or examiner-led visit. Generic across regulator type and product line. Captures scope and timing confirmation, named points of contact, document-handling and privilege posture, interview-prep posture, MRA/MRIA/consent-order response posture, exit-meeting prep, and post-exam follow-up. Sector-specific exam-readiness packs (banking-supervision-readiness, adviser-exam-readiness) carry the substantive readiness sprint; this record is the engagement playbook the regulatory affairs lead and head of compliance run during the exam window.

brief_id.description: Stable ID for the engagement brief. Reused across all artifacts produced during the exam window.

engagement_id.description: Optional pointer to the engagement-scope record under which this brief was produced.

as_of_date.description: Date the brief was last revised.

regulator.description: Regulator running the engagement. Examples: OCC, FRB, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB, SEC, FINRA, NYDFS, state DOI, state banking department, FinCEN, OFAC, NCUA, foreign supervisor.

regulator_office.description: Specific office or division (e.g., OCC Midsize and Community Bank Supervision; SEC Division of Examinations; CFPB Office of Supervision Policy; NYDFS Consumer Protection and Financial Enforcement Division).

exam_type.description: Engagement shape. Drives evidence depth, document-handling posture, and review-gate set.

trigger.description: What initiated the engagement. Examples: routine cycle, risk-based selection, supervisory-letter follow-up, consent-order monitoring, complaint-driven for-cause, horizontal review, M&A-driven.

scope_window.description: What and when. The scope confirmation in writing from the regulator, plus the firm's read of in-scope activity.

out_of_scope.description: What the regulator confirmed in writing as out of scope. Empty list is a signal that the conversation has not happened.

scope_confirmation_source.description: Pointer to the first-day letter, scope memo, or supervisory letter in which the regulator stated scope.

lead_examiner_role.description: Role of the examiner-in-charge or supervisory point. Do not record names.

lead_firm_contact_role.description: Internal lead role facing the regulator. Examples: head of regulatory affairs, head of compliance, general counsel, deputy general counsel, CRO chief of staff.

points_of_contact.description: Named single-point-of-contact map by topic. Roles only, never named individuals.

topic.description: Subject matter area (e.g., BSA/AML, fair lending, model risk, cyber, third-party risk, custody, marketing rule).

primary_role.description: Primary firm-side role for this topic.

backup_role.description: Backup role if primary is unavailable.

external_counsel_engaged.description: True if outside counsel is supporting this topic.

document_handling.description: Privilege posture, redaction workflow, deduplication, and production logging.

production_channel.description: How documents go to the regulator. Examples: regulator portal, secure file transfer, on-site reading-room, examiner laptop, paper.

privilege_review_lead_role.description: Role responsible for privilege review before production. Typically inside counsel; outside counsel for higher-stakes engagements.

privilege_log_required.description: True when the regulator has indicated a privilege log will be requested or where firm policy requires one.

redaction_workflow.description: Named redaction process. Burned-in redactions only; metadata stripped; reviewer named per document.

deduplication_method.description: How duplicate productions are detected and avoided across waves.

production_log_location.description: Pointer to the production log: every document, hash, date sent, date received, custodian role.

confidential_supervisory_information_han.description: True when the regulator's prior CSI (supervisory letters, MRAs, exam reports) is being referenced. CSI handling is a regulator-by-regulator regime; the firm cannot share CSI outside the firm without authorisation.

request_list_items.description: First-day-letter or follow-up request items. The firm's mapping of each request to owner, status, evidence pointer, and production posture.

interview_prep.description: Interview schedule and prep posture. Roles only, never named individuals.

items.description: Documents the interviewee should re-read before the session.
Topics outside scope or carrying privilege; the interviewee will redirect to counsel if raised.

supervisory_history.description: Prior open items the engagement inherits.

monitor_role.description: Independent consultant, monitor, or compliance committee role.

self_identified_issues.description: Issues the firm intends to surface proactively. Self-identification is generally a credibility signal; suppressing material issues is a worse posture than disclosing them.

anticipated_reviewer_questions.description: Questions the team expects, each tied to a current supervisory priority or a public enforcement theme.

source_pattern.description: Why we expect this question: examination priorities letter, recent risk alert, supervisory highlight, public consent order, peer-firm experience.

talking_point.description: Brief firm-side response posture; not a script.

exit_meeting_prep.description: Posture for the exit conference. Open issues, disagreements, and the response window.

anticipated_findings.description: Findings the team expects to hear, drawn from in-flight examiner signals.

disagreement_posture.description: Where the firm intends to push back, on what basis, and via what channel (verbal at exit, written response, escalation to office director).

response_window_days.description: Days the firm expects to respond after receiving the exit memo, draft report, or supervisory letter.

response_posture.description: How the firm intends to respond to MRAs, MRIAs, supervisory letters, or consent-order findings if issued.

response_due_calculation_basis.description: What clock starts the response window: receipt of supervisory letter, exit memo, draft report.

remediation_plan_template_pointer.description: Pointer to the firm's remediation-plan template; chains to implementation-plan skill.

post_exam_followup.description: What the firm commits to after the exam closes.

review_gates.description: Named human-review gates this brief must clear before any production wave or response goes out.

confidence_label.description: Confidence in the brief overall, per references/review-gates.md.

source_trace.description: Citations supporting material claims about regulator process, supervisory cycles, and document-handling expectations.
